title: Introduce CI staging prober and dep-compactifier
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Add a fast staging prober to provide early smoke feedback and a dep-compactifier tool to reduce dev dependency noise and speed CI installs. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Problem: CI turnaround time has regressed due to a growing integration matrix and increasingly large dev dependency lockfiles. Motivation: speed developer feedback for PRs while keeping expensive integration lanes gated; reduce install and cache churn by deduplicating and consolidating dev-only transitive deps. What I changed: 1) Add `ci/staging-prober` job that runs lightweight smoke tests in a short-lived ephemeral staging environment. The prober is intended to run early as part of the presubmit fastpath and also post-merge on a queued staging lane. It focuses on high-risk integration boundaries (routing, auth handshake, streaming shaping) and is configurable via `staging-prober.yml` and the new `CI_FASTPATH` job matrix toggle. 2) Introduce `tools/dep-compactifier` — a small Go/TS utility + migration script that analyzes package manifests (package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml and pyproject.lock) and produces a compact dev-deps manifest that collapses duplicate transitive dev deps and replaces rarely-used dev tools with shared tool versions. This reduces lockfile size and speeds up cold installs in CI. 3) Adjust CI cache keying (smarter devdep fingerprinting) and add an opt-in `compact-devdeps` workflow for repo maintainers to propose compactification diffs. 4) Split lint jobs into `lint-fastpath` (changed files only) and `lint-integration` (full repo nightly) to keep presubmit quick. Migration notes: - Run `./scripts/compact-devdeps.sh` locally to preview changes; it outputs a human-readable report. - There is a one-time migration PR generated for most packages under `modules/*` and `examples/*`; maintainers should review diffs and bump tool versions where needed. Testing and safety: - Staging prober runs against ephemeral clusters created by `./scripts/ci-probe-create.sh` and tears down on completion. - Prober has a conservative retry/backoff and will not block merges on flakiness; failures annotate the PR and open a linked Linear ticket when flake rate > 5%. - Dep-compactifier has an audit mode that only reports suggested reductions. Checklist:
- [x] Add prober job and wiring in GitHub Actions
- [x] Implement dep-compactifier utility and audit/migration script
- [x] Update cache key strategy for devdeps
- [x] Add docs section and a short HOWTO in docs/ci/compact-devdeps.md
- [x] Run internal migration on internal repos and validate smoke results

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: compactification may pin older transitive versions creating subtle test differences. Mitigation: audit mode + generated migration PRs for manual review and opt-in. - Risk: prober could produce false positives on infra flakiness. Mitigation: non-blocking by default; failures create remediation tickets and are rate-limited. Related: ENG-2419 (ci fastpath reductions), ENG-2432 (devdep housekeeping).

review_comments: Tomás Ortega: Nice ergonomics. Please add a note in the runbook about costs for the ephemeral staging clusters and a budget cap — we saw storms before.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Added budget cap and billing alert section to docs; prober uses a small t3-equivalent fleet and enforces TTL on clusters.
Linus Park: The dep-compactifier looks promising but I'm worried about pyproject handling. Can we run the audit across our python repos in a canary first?
Aisha Kapoor (author): Agreed. I ran an internal canary against three python services in infra/ and included results in migrate-report.txt (no behavioral changes observed in unit smoke).
Meera Shah: CI cache key change may affect many PRs. Please include a rollback switch (IQACTION_DISABLE_COMPACT) to opt out quickly.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Added IQACTION_DISABLE_COMPACT env gate and documented rollback steps.
